/* gallerysection.css — DERIVED FROM /gallery's own sheets. Do not edit by hand.

   SKRIBL'S OWN GALLERY, ON A PAGE THAT IS NOT SKRIBL'S (the owner's B, after
   v330: "one gallery, two doors"). A host's page holds the Gallery section
   (_skribl_gallery_section.html: skribl_gallery_assets() and
   skribl_gallery_section()) and loads this one sheet for it, beside the
   player's own (skribl_inline_assets()). /gallery itself never loads it: it
   keeps its <style> and its component sheets, untouched.

   WHAT IS IN IT. The rules /gallery styles the section with, one by one, in
   the order /gallery loads them: fullband.css (the full screen), fullbar.css
   (the card's bar), tooltip.css, labels.css, pagemenu.css's glass and grab bar
   (only those: the rest of it is the page's header and its ••• menu),
   segslider.css (New / Hot), and skribl_gallery.html's own <style>.

   NOTHING LEAKS OUT. Every selector is written under the section's root,
   #skriblGallery, so no rule here can match the host's own page. Two are
   about the page itself, and only while Skribl says so on <html>: a drawing
   full screen holds the page still (html.skribl-immersive), and after a
   pointer the section's focus rings step back (html[data-input]).

   NOTHING LEAKS IN. The root starts from nothing (all: initial) and takes
   what /gallery's page gives the section: its body's type, its ink, the
   browser's size, and its <html>'s language. Every part of it starts from the
   browser's own defaults (all: revert), as it does on /gallery, before the
   rules below; an id outweighs every rule a page writes with classes and
   elements, so a host's `.btn`, its `.tabs`, its `button` or its `h2` cannot
   add to what the section shows. The player's box keeps inlineplayer.css,
   which every host page loads, and an <svg> or a <canvas> keeps what its
   attributes say (a revert would undo those too). And
   every custom property the section reads is the section's: the ones
   /gallery's root defines are defined on this root, both themes, and the rest
   are cut off at it (initial), so a host's name cannot reach in either.

   LIGHT AND DARK. /gallery's light theme is :root[data-theme="light"], which
   a host that stamps data-theme on <html> also says. A host that follows the
   device instead (prefers-color-scheme) and sets no data-theme gets the same
   light rules through the media query, beside each one.

   THE COST IS DUPLICATION, paid for by an assertion: verify_seam.py, on every
   pull request, regenerates this file and fails if it differs by one byte
   from what those sheets produce. A rule edited on /gallery and not re-emitted
   here is a red suite; the one command that re-emits player.css re-emits this
   too:  python3 harness/tools/cssgraph.py --emit harness/tools/css_live.json
   skribl/static/player.css */
